items.stem: An item has a gross requirement of 100, on-hand 30 and no scheduled receipts. What is the net requirement before lot sizing?

options.rationale: Correct: net requirement = gross (100) - on-hand (30) - scheduled receipts (0) = 70.
30 is the on-hand balance, not the net requirement.

items.stem: The primary purpose of sales and operations planning (S&OP) is to:

options.text: Align demand and supply plans across functions at an aggregate level
options.rationale: Correct: S&OP aligns demand and supply across functions at an aggregate, medium-term level.

options.text: Schedule individual machines by the hour
options.rationale: That is detailed scheduling, below the S&OP horizon.
S&OP informs but is not the accounting budget process.
Packaging is an execution detail, not S&OP's purpose.

items.explanation: S&OP aligns demand and supply across functions at an aggregate level.

items.stem: A plant wants to reduce finished-goods inventory without hurting service. Select TWO actions consistent with lean inventory practice.

options.text: Reduce replenishment lot sizes and setup times
options.rationale: Correct: smaller lots with faster setups cut average inventory while protecting flow.

options.text: Improve forecast accuracy to lower required safety stock
options.rationale: Correct: better forecasts reduce the safety stock needed for a given service level.

options.text: Increase batch sizes to gain economies of scale
options.rationale: Larger batches raise average inventory, the opposite of the goal.

options.text: Add a second safety-stock buffer at every node
Lengthen supplier lead times to smooth ordering
options.rationale: Longer lead times require more, not less, inventory.

items.explanation: Smaller lots/faster setups and better forecasts both cut inventory without hurting service.
